# Expected — 07 gift-card-licensing

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | scam |
| Family | Jobs |
| Expected label | **Scam markers: 4 or more** |
| Recovery branch | no |
| Purpose | The untraceable-payment pattern in its casual register: chat-app supervisor, gift cards, photos of codes — tests the kit on short, informal messages, not just emails |

## Markers that MUST appear (each quoted from the message)

| Category | Must quote |
|---|---|
| Payment shape | "buy 3 gift cards of $200 each… send clear photos of the codes" — gift cards are the untraceable ask |
| Information extraction | the photos of the codes themselves — the thing that makes the money unrecoverable |
| Isolation | the whole exchange lives in Telegram ("send clear photos of the codes here") |
| Urgency | "If you can get them today, your first shift is tomorrow" |
| Process anomaly | software licensing issued through retail gift cards — no real company licenses that way |

## Markers that must NOT appear

- Authority costume — no brand is borrowed; do not invent one.

## Guards

- The register changes (emoji, first name, chat format) but the rules do not: the report stays plain and calm, no mockery of the tone.
- The [CONFIRM] discipline holds: nothing about "Lena" or the company is asserted beyond the text.
- Verify checklist fits the format: no real employer collects license fees in gift cards — the check is the company's real existence and channel.
